question: According to widely circulating estimates, in Europe around 2 200 000 people died due to COVID-19, in tragic circumstances. Many Member States have already paid tribute to the victims and to all those who stepped up to care for them and, above all, to save lives.

There is a lack of clarity on the way the pandemic was handled, including the way the vaccination campaign was managed, and on the imposing, sometimes even in the form of blackmail, of experimental gene serums placed on the market with a conditional authorisation.

Many doctors raised doubts over the sense of the vaccination campaign, and over shortcomings, errors and mismanagement, and over measures at odds with the law and with medical science. There was a lack of transparency over the contracts with the pharmaceutical companies, which were cloaked in ‘military’ secrecy.

Consideration was given to studies that had no scientific value, but which were vitiated by receiving funding from companies with major vested interests, without those really to blame being investigated. In view of the above, can the Commission state why a European Day to commemorate the victims of the poor handling of COVID-19 has not yet been established?
answer: The Commission has actively supported Member States in coordinating their response to the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2020, the Commission presented the EU Vaccines Strategy (1) and a communication on COVID-19 vaccination (2). According to the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU, Union action shall respect the responsibilities of Member States for the definition of their health policy.

During public health emergencies, a conditional marketing authorisation (CMA) allows to authorise a medicine on less comprehensive data than normally required, where the benefit of its immediate availability outweighs its risks.

The COVID-19 vaccines’ CMAs were converted into standard authorisations following the submission of additional data, particularly based on the vaccines’ successful use in hundreds of millions of people worldwide.

Concerning transparency, the Commission has published the contracts signed for the purchase of COVID-19 vaccines, with redactions to respect the right of the contractors to protect their commercial interests (3). The Commission has also provided replies to requests for access to documents under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 (4) on the topic and has released several documents in this context (5).
The Commission has taken note of the proposal to establish a European Day of Remembrance for the victims of COVID-19 and will consider it, in cooperation with the Member States.
